title: Charlie Irvis, Bubber Miley and the New York origin of the growl
summary: The five-piece band added trombonist Charlie Irvis, who invented the growl on trombone, and Bubber Miley; both were New Yorkers.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: How large was the band at that time?

Five pieces when they were at the Kentucky Club. Yes, five pieces. Then they added on a trombone player name of Charlie Irvis who did the plunger bit, the Tricky Sam, he created that. There was a fellow came from St. Louis did the wah-wah, the first one we heard do the plunger bit that Johnny Dunn had created back in 1920, and then invented the plunger. A fellow by the name of Jonas Walker came from St. Louis to New York and the trombone players heard him, so Charlie Irvis got some part of a little tin mute he used to use and did that growling, so he was the first trombone player with Duke before Tricky Sam, and -- but that's how the growl came about, Charlie Irvis. He was a New York kid too. And Bubber Miley was the other -- when they put the second trumpet on they put Bubber Miley in there, and he was also a New Yorker. So the two -- really the strong influences in Duke's band are native New Yorkers. Yes, they were.
Is that right? Was Duke, when he first came out, after Sonny Greer made the switch for him, and came out as Duke Ellington's Band, was the name of it -- overnight it was Duke Ellington's Band, right?
